definition: A system component that directs incoming requests to different models (or model configurations) based on factors like task complexity, cost constraints, or required capability.
details: Model routing allows applications to balance cost and performance by sending simpler queries to smaller, cheaper models and reserving larger, more capable (and expensive) models for harder tasks.

explainer.lead: A component that sends incoming requests to different models or configurations based on task complexity, cost constraints, or required capability. It lets applications balance cost and performance.

tiers.eli5: Like a receptionist who sends simple questions to a junior clerk and hard ones to a senior expert.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers route simple queries to smaller, cheaper models and reserve larger, more capable ones for harder tasks. A pitfall is misjudging task difficulty, so hard queries land on weak models and quality drops.
tiers.paperLevel: A router maps each request to a model or configuration using criteria such as complexity, cost, or capability; routing accuracy bounds the achievable quality-cost trade-off.

explainer.example: A support app sends greetings to a small cheap model and multi-step troubleshooting requests to a large model.
